Prevention: Use tolerant varieties against this disease: "Red
Apple" variety is good to reduce disease
Prune and remove dried shoots at the end of the season
Get rid of apples in the trees if there are too many.
Remove fallen leaves and weeds from the field at the end of the season to prevent disease staying in the field during the dormant period
Do not let the field get too humid
Monitoring: From mid-May, observe the field once a week and look for the symptoms: on the leaves, silvery grey powder on the lower leaf surface and some yellow spots on the upper leaf surface.
The fruit may be distorted or discoloured and reduces the quality of the fruit
Problems are found on the dormant tree, and it grows onto new shoots when they grow in the spring: look for silvery grey powder and early defoliation
When the problem starts in the field, start control measures soon afterwards, as the disease can grow quickly
Direct Control: Prune and remove dried and infected shoots, and destroy outside the field.
Spray of urea at 5kg /100L water when 60-70% leaves are fallen
Use wettable sulphur solution @ 3-4 g/litre of water
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
During the use of pesticides, prevent children and animals from entering the field and do not eat drink or smoke whilst using chemicals of any kind
Change your clothes and wash your body and face after using chemicals
Keep pesticides out of reach of children
Lime sulphur is slightly hazardous; Class
III; may be harmful if swallowed or absorbed through the skin.
Spray during dormant stage in winter.
Spray when the temperature is below 30 degrees celsius.
Mancozeb is unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use, Class
Spray in 20 day intervals; 2-3 applications per season
